commodity_commentary: Commodity markets were led higher this week by energy, where WTI crude rose 4.97% to US$100.16/bbl and Brent gained 7.21% to US$108.59/bbl, both driven by Strait of Hormuz supply disruption flagged in the May IEA Oil Market Report.20 Natural gas added 5.88% to US$2.92/MMBtu while remaining 14.82% below a year ago. Precious metals diverged from energy: gold fell 3.33% to US$4,563.20/oz and silver eased 2.00% to US$78.79/oz, though gold held a 39.1% year-over-year gain after record Q1 2026 global demand reported by the World Gold Council33. Base metals firmed, with copper up 1.47% to US$6.34/lb on resilient Chinese demand after Q1 2026 GDP printed 5.0%25. Agriculture moved with wheat up 7.82% to 655.00c/bu and potash up 4.34% on the Nutrien proxy; lumber added 1.39% to US$584.50/mfbm. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the energy move to 59 oil and gas projects ($97.6B) and the metals strength to the resource pipeline within the database's 7,480 tracked projects valued at $1,472.2B14. Western Canadian Select, uranium, nickel and canola carried no priced series in the data this week and are marked unavailable.

commodities.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
commodities.context: Crude Oil (WTI): US$100.16/bbl (+4.97% week-over-week) — crude climbed back toward US$100 following reports of a Trump-Xi discussion of the Strait of Hormuz, with the May IEA Oil Market Report framing the supply-shock backdrop1920. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the move to 59 oil and gas projects valued at $97.6B, connected to the crude-led March trade surplus. If WTI holds near US$100/bbl, those 59 oil and gas projects would retain netbacks well above the levels implied by the US$70.70/bbl trailing one-year average, with the price now 60.10% above its year-ago level and within the US$55.27-US$112.95/bbl 52-week range14.

commodities.name: Western Canadian Select
commodities.context: Western Canadian Select: N/A — Data unavailable for this commodity this week. No WCS price or WCS/WTI differential series was carried in the data this run, so the WCS discount calculation and heavy-crude netback analysis are not reported.

commodities.name: Crude Oil (Brent)
commodities.context: Crude Oil (Brent): US$108.59/bbl (+7.21% week-over-week) — the global benchmark outpaced WTI on the Hormuz supply disruption, widening to 66.09% above its year-ago level, the largest 12-month gain among tracked energy contracts and near the upper end of its US$58.92-US$118.35/bbl 52-week range20.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.context: Natural Gas: US$2.92/MMBtu (+5.88% week-over-week) — Henry Hub firmed on the broader energy-complex move tied to the Hormuz disruption, yet remained 14.82% below its year-ago level and beneath its US$3.28/MMBtu trailing one-year average, a level relevant to LNG export economics and feed-gas-linked projects in the database19. The price held well off the US$7.46/MMBtu 52-week high and above the US$1.64/MMBtu 52-week low.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.context: Gold: US$4,563.20/oz (-3.33% week-over-week) — bullion eased as the energy-led move pulled flows toward crude, though it held a 39.11% year-over-year gain following record Q1 2026 global gold demand reported by the World Gold Council and continued central-bank buying3334. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine connects the price to mining projects within the tracked pipeline; the level sits below the US$5,318.40/oz 52-week high but well above the US$3,659.87/oz one-year average.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.context: Silver: US$78.79/oz (-2.00% week-over-week) — silver eased following the pullback in gold as energy-complex flows drew capital toward crude, but retained a 138.90% year-over-year gain, the largest 12-month move of any tracked commodity, against a US$29.51-US$115.08/oz 52-week range.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.context: Copper: US$6.34/lb (+1.47% week-over-week) — copper firmed on resilient Chinese demand after Q1 2026 GDP printed 5.0%, supporting electrification and base-metals mining projects in the database25. The price is 37.27% above its year-ago level and near the US$6.64/lb 52-week high, well above the US$4.99/lb one-year average.

commodities.name: Uranium
commodities.context: Uranium: N/A — Data unavailable for this commodity this week. No spot uranium series was carried in the data this run; Saskatchewan uranium project exposure is referenced qualitatively only.

commodities.name: Nickel
commodities.context: Nickel: N/A — Data unavailable for this commodity this week. Only a single spot datapoint (about US$17,076/t) was carried, with no computable weekly, monthly or year-over-year deltas, so no price move is published.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.context: Wheat: 655.00c/bu (+7.82% week-over-week) — wheat advanced as the Middle East conflict lifting global input costs fed into grain markets, and now stands 19.96% above its year-ago level at the top of its 495.00-665.00c/bu 52-week range, relevant to Prairie agriculture and grain-handling projects in the pipeline.

commodities.name: Canola
commodities.context: Canola: N/A — Data unavailable for this commodity this week. No canola series was carried in the data this run; Prairie oilseed exposure is referenced qualitatively only.

commodities.name: Potash (Nutrien)
commodities.context: Potash (Nutrien): US$97.34 (+4.34% week-over-week, Nutrien proxy) — the potash proxy gained amid the firm global fertilizer demand backdrop and is 20.28% above its year-ago level, within a US$72.29-US$114.41 52-week range, relevant to Saskatchewan fertilizer projects in the database.

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.context: Lumber: US$584.50/mfbm (+1.39% week-over-week) — lumber edged up but remained 3.39% below its year-ago level and essentially in line with its US$583.50/mfbm one-year average, as CMHC March housing starts fell 6% month-over-month, a construction-input read tied to BC forestry and residential projects in the database16. The price held below the US$695.50/mfbm 52-week high.
